title: Claude gains infinite memory via Notebook LM integration #claudeai #persistentmemory #aitechnology
description: Claude gained infinite memory by integrating with Google’s Notebook LM, allowing persistent memory across sessions without consuming extra tokens. This connection uses a wrap-up skill that saves conversations automatically and enables semantic search for relevant context retrieval. This approach reduces token costs dramatically by avoiding repeated context loading, while enriching responses with infographics, cinematic videos, and deep research embedded within Notebook LM. It transforms Claude into a more efficient and knowledgeable assistant for ongoing tasks. The innovation highlights the potential of combining AI chat models with external research platforms to enhance user experience and lower operational costs in natural language processing workflows. #ClaudeAI #NotebookLM #GoogleResearch #AIMemory #SemanticSearch #TokenOptimization #AIAssistants #ConversationalAI #AIIntegration #AIEfficiency #NaturalLanguageProcessing #AIResearchTools #MachineLearning #OpenAIAlternatives #AIVideoGeneration

top_comments.author: @morris5984
top_comments.text: Since neither Claude or Notebook LM have a direct integration, I can only assume this is a third-party MCP server where someone  reverse engineered Notebook LM’s API endpoints. Notebook LM does NOT expose a public API.  If Google changes their code that breaks the 3rd party hacked API, Google won’t support fixing it and those that use it will be SOL until it’s hacked again.  I would stick with an open sourced vector database (free and supported) if you are looking to have “unlimited memory” and reduce token usage without relying on something that may or may not work tomorrow. If your not familiar with Vector DBs (Qdrant, Weaviat to name a couple), plenty of helpful information is out there or just ask Claude!
